$comment: Producer productization and first-wave consumer-install sequence. Not a live lifecycle-position table, not a publication catalogue, and not permission to install every package. Membership is the nineteen current source packages; order is engagement, then operational integrity, then expression. Runtime edges are read from package manifests at check time, not restated here. A consumer still opens only justified positions and skips not-applicable roles.

nonRuntimeOrder.reason: Audience-response measurement is the learn stage of publication; productizing influencer before publisher designs an open loop.

waves.job: Make every current identity anonymously installable and honestly documented before any first-wave consumer is told to pin it.
Reconcile sponsor intent, readiness, and first-wave pre-work before any operating position is opened.
Prove the consumer-owned trusted-base foundation and activation path without treating executable tooling as a role.
Make operating rules expressible, current, and followable; this is the runtime root for later operating packages.
Productize the independent measurer, topology, change judgment, live-state realization, key custody, and package-currency loops before any expression or frontend work.
Productize authority, intent confirmation, transport, obligation discharge, and holding-stewardship loops for person-facing operating integrity.

Productize strategy, copy, design, verified publication, then audience-response learning. Designer and publisher are last among expression because they are frontend surfaces; publisher still waits for writer and designer at runtime.

productizationCriteria.means: The role declares one job question, one owned metric, one primary mode, a durable boundary, and a close condition.
Every declared bin runs when invoked through the installer-linked name, not only when spawned by real path. A bin that exits 0 with no output on every input is not staged evidence.

The package README names the public npm registry and states that current-scope install needs no token. A GitHub Packages token instruction on a public-npm package is a blocking defect. A missing public-npm claim is counted, not a pass over unexamined ground.

The package README states the close condition a consumer binds. The shared charter string stays consumer-owned. Advisor is the first README that must state one; remaining packages are the supplier gap tracked in #906.
The owned metric is computed by shipped code under the name the charter declares. A declaration with no computation, or a computation of a different metric, is an open loop.
The installed CLI produces native 0, 1, and 2 from matched fixtures, with a control that stays green in the same run.
This repository can invoke the package by dist path, and a consumer can re-run the same CLI or export from an exact pin without a second unpublished path.
A first-day role declares foundry.assessment against a mapped bin. Orchestration never infers one. Advisor is the first role that must have one.

backlogRouting.matches: Source/registry drift, contaminated latest tarball, missing current-version qualification, dead installer-linked bins, install docs that demand a token for public npm, or a check that reports success over ground it never examined on a consumer-facing bin.
A defect, missing criterion, or closed-loop gap named against one current package. Route it to that package's wave; do not pull an expression package forward to fix an operating package.
Visual, RTL, composition, dogfood application, or audience-surface work. These wait until operational-integrity waves are productized.
Work that can only be evidenced in a consuming repository: pinning, wiring, deliberate failure, duplicate deletion, outcome measurement. Foundry can unblock it; it cannot finish it.
A candidate role that is not one of the nineteen current packages. Record it; do not sequence it in front of first-wave productization of the current catalogue.
A/B/C programme plans, superseded publication-order trackers, or any issue whose orientation command or position table no longer exists. Do not use them as the session entry point.
